correctness.rationale: Roman domination is monotone under pointwise label increases, so local one-coordinate decreases suffice for minimality. Fixing X as the core vertices labeled 2 forces (2,0) at X, (0,1) on the external neighborhood N(X)\X, and independently (0,2) or (1,1) on each vertex outside N[X]; local zero-defender checks prove both necessity and sufficiency. The resulting weight is 2n-|N(X)\X|=n+|X|+|V\N[X]| and multiplicity 2^{|V\N[X]|} for every finite simple H. Counting independent subsets of a bipartite neighborhood double corresponds to choosing X and an arbitrary subset of V\N[X]. Minimum exponent n+gamma(H) follows because X union unexposed is dominating; maximum coefficient is product over components (2^{|Q|}+1) by zero boundary. Four-case bipartite-base specialization follows from the same sum. Independent direct brute enumeration for H=K2 gives 2 z^3+5 z^4. This is a universal structural proof, not an extrapolation from checks.
